chains.note: x402 settlement via the public facilitator

chains.name: Base
chains.note: mainnet settlement — facilitator key + funded wallet flips it live

chains.name: Arc Testnet
chains.note: Circle's USDC-native L1 — USDC is the gas token; this address is its ERC-20 interface (6 decimals over an 18-decimal native balance). Full v2 wiring; goes live when a configured facilitator names eip155:5042002

chains.name: Solana Devnet
chains.note: x402 settlement via the public facilitator — real second signature scheme, not just a second EVM chain

chains.name: Aptos Testnet
chains.note: x402 settlement via the public facilitator — Move account model, third signature family

chains.name: Stellar Testnet
chains.note: x402 settlement via the public facilitator — fees sponsored by the facilitator itself

chains.name: Hedera Testnet
chains.note: x402 settlement via the public facilitator — account-id addressing (0.0.x), not a keypair-derived address; needs a real registered testnet account, an ephemeral keypair alone can't settle

chains.name: Algorand Testnet
chains.note: the public facilitator settles this network and sponsors the fee, but no @x402/algorand client scheme package is published yet — governed here, not signable here

chains.name: XRPL
chains.note: x402 v2 wiring is real, but mainnet settlement is DISABLED by default — simulate mode (the default) never touches it, and testnet mode requires an operator to explicitly set SERVER_PAYOUT_ADDRESS_XRPL to enable it. This is real mainnet, real money, RLUSD not USDC (XRPL has no canonical USDC deployment) — an operator who enables it does so entirely at their own risk; we do not run, control, or monitor anyone's deployment

chains.name: Cardano Preprod
chains.note: x402 added Cardano support 2026-09-09 and @x402/cardano is now on npm (2.27.0), but the public facilitator doesn't list a cardano network yet and this instance doesn't wire the scheme — governed here, not settleable here

packs.name: cautious
packs.$description: Tight training wheels: tiny caps, everything above a cent needs a human, hair-trigger runaway freeze, spending pinned to the one live chain. Start every new agent fleet here.

packs.name: production
packs.$description: For fleets you already trust: higher throughput, approvals reserved for genuinely large spends, runaway guard still armed, spending pinned to the Base chains. Set alertWebhookUrl before using this one.

packs.name: standard
packs.$description: The shipped default: sensible caps, human sign-off on anything above $0.015, 10-attempts-in-10s runaway freeze.

packs.name: trading
packs.$description: For trading desks: tight per-trade caps, two approvers above the position threshold, a hair-trigger runaway freeze, and a UTC trading window (edit allowedHoursUTC to your session — shipped wide open so nothing surprises you on day one).

rails.name: x402 — simulated settlement
rails.note: real ECDSA + replay protection; settles locally on all 7 registered chains

rails.name: x402 v2 — live settlement
rails.note: real on-chain USDC/stablecoin settlement on every registry chain the configured facilitator supports (public facilitator: base-sepolia, solana-devnet, aptos-testnet, stellar-testnet, hedera-testnet, and XRPL mainnet today; CDP facilitator key unlocks EVM mainnets)

rails.name: Safe{Wallet} AllowanceModule
rails.note: on-chain-enforced spend caps via Safe's audited AllowanceModule — real call path implemented, gated behind SAFE_ADDRESS/ALLOWANCE_MODULE_ADDRESS config; see docs/safe-allowance.md
